subject: The reviewed offline Restricted boundary and its tests, with live installation held
reader: Parker knows Terminal Delight and raised the rogue-process concern, but does not read Rust and was away from the implementation

sections.heading: Restricted commands
sections.text: A build from an unfamiliar repository can run beside a production shell. Both belong to you, but the build should not gain control of that shell. Restricted starts the build with one chosen project and no network. This review fixes the reported gaps and records what the tests cover.

sections.heading: Shared workspace
sections.text:
01 · One owner, different reach 

 Standard terminal 
Normal account access.
Production shell, private files, online tools. 
 Restricted command 
One project at /work .
Offline tools and temporary scratch space. 
 Online Restricted agent 
Unavailable.
Product and architecture drafts only. 
 Standard remains the compatibility choice; Restricted is an explicit launch. An off-limits pane mark controls TD disclosure and does not sandbox its programs. Drawn from the implemented CLI and permission policy. 
That leaves two boundaries to verify: which files the command receives, and which TD actions it can request.

sections.heading: Directory identity
sections.text:
The review found that validation pinned one directory but scanned its pathname. Renaming that path could make the scan inspect a replacement. Validation now walks open directory handles and checks each entry’s device and mount identity. 
 02 · Follow the pinned tree 

 Before the fix 
- Pin project A. 
- A moves; clean B takes its name. 
- Scan B, then mount A. 
 Now 
- Pin project A. 
- Walk A through its open handles. 
- Refuse a replaced root or nested mount. 
 Both pin/scan swap tests refuse launch, and a real same-device bind mount is refused before the command starts. These are test observations, not an estimate of every possible host race. A malicious host process remains outside the protection direction. 
 03 · The work-root rule is predictable 

ALLOW ~/Projects/example 
GRANTED CONTENT ~/Projects/example/.git and other files inside it 
REFUSE ~/.aws , ~/.kube/project , hidden selected paths 
REFUSE system trees and external volumes such as /mnt/disk 
 Select a non-hidden directory below the OS account home. Copy outside work into a dedicated project. Secrets already in that project, supplied arguments and stdin are granted content. The rule follows the canonical path: a volume mounted below an allowed home path belongs to the selected grant. Nested mounts within it are refused. 
The command’s access to TD needs its own check.

sections.heading: Caller identity
sections.text:
An agent could previously name another pane and be treated as its occupant. The OS now reports which process connected to TD. TD checks that process runs under the pane it claims, then checks the current policy before making a change. A Restricted command uses a supervisor outside its sandbox to relay its permitted note. 
 04 · Check the caller, then the current policy 

 A forged pane claim loses its own-pane exception. A real relay and Restricted supervisor still work. Surfaces are saved only after UI acceptance; a stale snapshot cannot leave a refused card for the later sweep. Diagram follows the actual request path. 
 05 · Hidden still permits its own work | 
 | Scratch native exercise | Observed 
 | Genuine caller: own hidden note, document open and notes read | Allowed 
 | Forged caller: note, deliverable, surface, request and document read | Refused 
 | Foreign document/Workbench routes; hidden-tab edits by PID or index | Hidden target protected 
 | Ordinary window: all six MCP policy mutations | Refused 
 These checks run against the application in isolated native windows. Config-field injection and queued input have additional behavioral tests. Picker routing is mutation-tested in the native window, rather than inferred from a source-text search.

sections.heading: Access proposals
sections.text:
06 · One proposal, no grant 
 RESTRICTED ACCESS PROPOSAL — workload request, no access granted 
Current resource: chosen project (read-write)
Request supplied by workload: “Need external packages”
Consequence: changing scope requires a separately chosen new run. terminal-delight restricted dismiss RUN 
 The supervisor prints one proposal in the run terminal. Outside-only dismissal clears it without resetting that run’s proposal budget. The workload cannot dismiss or approve it. A real OS test checks visibility, refusal and unchanged grants. The attention rail is not connected to this profile. 

The optional own-note grant still follows the existing MCP switches. Revocation blocks future TD effects after an in-flight accepted note finishes; it does not undo files or stop ongoing file work. Network, TUIs, GUI services and automatic delegation remain unavailable.

sections.heading: Regression controls
sections.text:
Removing each protection independently checks whether its regression test can detect the failure. The first injection fixtures could not: their invalid payloads were refused before reaching the intended guard. Correcting those fixtures made both removed guards fail their intended tests. 
 07 · Actual evidence and limits 

 2670 
Default-core checks passed.
15 ignored, reported separately. 
 2617 
Fallback-core checks passed.
15 ignored, reported separately. 
 5 real OS probes 
Explicitly invoked.
Useful work and attempted boundary crossings. 

 21 independent mutations caught 
One protection removed at a time, with baseline and exact-byte restoration controls. Compiler failures do not count. 
 Coverage has limits 
ARM runtime qualification is unmeasured. Complete resource quotas, hostile host users and kernel exploits are outside this qualification. 
 Every reproduced escape or broken allowed workflow adds a permanent regression case. Passing this corpus measures these paths; it never makes the threat model complete. Receipts name the source fingerprint, binary digest, commands and logs. Earlier mixed-source evidence is archived as historical. 

Both strict production lint runs, formatting, the optimized build and remote CI pass. The native exercise also checks the older host binary used by the existing daily window. Authorized output and shared files can still mislead an unrestricted reader; that reader’s broader actions are outside the boundary. 
 Open the source and reproducible evidence 
 The security review completion · Portable reproducers · Current receipt · User guide 
The development receipt records the tested source file map and exact binary digest. Its full raw logs remain in the local operational archive; the repository includes the commands, summaries and individual mutation controls. 
The installable local candidate also preserves the daily build’s existing palette and note previews. It has its own qualification receipt and digest: its source is the reviewed development code plus those existing previews, not a claim that the two trees are identical. 
The candidate receipt records its separate source map and binary digest. Its full suites: 2672 default and 2619 fallback tests passed, with ignored tests separate in the receipt. Both native exercises pass against these exact candidate bytes.

sections.heading: Held installation
sections.text:
08 · Ready without replacing the live window 

 Completed 
One review completion for 0.5 development.
Current-source tests and portable evidence.
Offline user guide and visible proposals. 
 Held as instructed 
The live daily window still uses the earlier Restricted build.
These review fixes await installation.
0.4 releases and agent-management integration are separate. 
 Scratch qualification leaves the daily window in place. The installation command below is for after review. No claim of a new release or candidate hold is made. 

# Install for future launches, after review
python3 /home/parker/.cache/td-security-finish/wt/reports/restricted-commands-proof/install-candidate.py --candidate /home/parker/.cache/td-security-finish/artifacts/td-f5b9a6791418-restricted-review --sha256 8edf3b15bdacfec3035d759c16817ba32fef167ec82d2fee0bf8b340ea3307bd --expected-launcher /home/parker/.local/lib/terminal-delight/td-3ff49b8e-0.5-restricted --apply

# Undo a later selection
python3 /home/parker/.cache/td-security-finish/wt/reports/restricted-commands-proof/install-candidate.py --candidate /home/parker/.local/lib/terminal-delight/td-3ff49b8e-0.5-restricted --sha256 3b9165e704c951c55801fee10244b4a00a277049a71804f46adce9c9d6c2c3a4 --expected-launcher /home/parker/.local/lib/terminal-delight/td-f5b9a6791418-restricted-review --apply 

The install command selects the reviewed candidate for future launches; the undo command selects the previous binary again. Both keep the versioned files. Omit --apply to inspect first. Save work and use the normal close/reopen path when ready; the installer never reloads a running window.
